# Apex Construction

> Apex Construction is a general contractor and custom home builder in Austin, Texas — commercial construction, custom homes, remodeling, design-build, and civil sitework delivered across Central Texas with fixed-price discipline and weekly reporting.

Apex Construction runs its own sites, employs its own crews, and has delivered 400+ projects since 2001 — commercial build-outs, ground-up custom homes, whole-house remodels, and site infrastructure. Licensed (TX GC Lic. #42-8137), bonded, and insured, with an EMR safety rating of 0.98.

## Frequently asked questions

- Where does Apex Construction work? Austin and Central Texas — Travis, Williamson, Hays, and Bastrop counties. Commercial projects are accepted statewide by arrangement.
- Are you licensed and insured? Yes — TX GC Lic. #42-8137, bonded, with general liability and workers' compensation coverage on every project.
- Do you offer design-build or just construction? Both. About half of our work is design-build; we also build from architect-ready plans for bid-build projects.
- How do I get a quote? Request a consultation at https://apexconstruction.com/quote, or add services to a brief from https://apexconstruction.com/services. We respond within one business day and schedule a site walk before numbers are finalized.
- How much does a custom home cost in Austin? Typically starting around $375 per square foot for simpler programs; a pre-construction agreement produces a real number for your lot and program.
- How long does a custom home take? Design and permitting four to seven months; construction ten to fourteen months for most programs.
- Is a fixed-price contract really fixed? Yes. Allowances are itemized to the fixture level, and the only way the price changes is a change order you sign.
- How are payments structured? Milestone-based draw schedules tied to completed, inspected work — never deposits for future work.
- Who handles permits? Apex prepares, submits, and manages permits through the city or county having jurisdiction.
- What happens if the schedule slips? You hear it from us first, with the recovery plan in the same conversation. Weekly reports keep schedule risk visible before it becomes slip.
